doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Arranging and style in the Basie band
title: His relationship with Basie
summary: Their contact was mostly about arrangements, and Foster called him Chief or Bas with deep respect.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Interesting. Over time, how did your relationship with Basie develop? You fall into your imitation of him, how you look up and where you’re throwing your voice, but talk about how your relationship evolved with Basie, the interaction. Was he always with you just a person of few words and gestures? Did there come a time when you had access to him on another level, where he talked about things?
Mostly when I had access to him on other levels, so to speak, we might be talking about an arrangement he wanted me to do.

Yeah. Then he would be detailed in a simplistic manner. He’d say, kid take it here. Do this and so and so. Then I want this little figure in there [Foster sings a melody]. Then have a little piano solo. Then shoot yourself in there a little bit. Give yourself some action. Then have this little [Foster sings a brief melody]. Then the rest of it, go for yourself. Do what you want to do on the ending”.
He’d done about 80 percent of it [laughter].

This relationship was very -- I had a very wonderful relationship with the Chief. It got to the point where I felt at ease calling him Chief or Bas, although I was always -- even up to the time I gave him my notice that I was leaving the band, I was always in awe of him and always respectful.
